title: Length, Mass and Capacity
seo_title: Grade 2 Length, Mass and Capacity Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Length, mass and capacity: estimate, measure, compare and order using informal units and standard units: metres (length), kilograms (mass) and litres (capacity).
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 2 maths worksheets: measuring length in cm and m, mass in kg and capacity in litres, rulers and scales. 100 questions with pictures and memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Start measuring at the 0 on the ruler.
  • Use cm for short things and m for long things.
  • Mass is measured in kilograms (kg); capacity in litres (ℓ).
  • Read the scale: count the steps between the numbered marks.

Examples

Example

A pencil from 0 to 15 on a ruler

read the end

Answer: 15 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Starting at 1Start at 0.
The wrong unitA classroom is metres, not centimetres.
Between marksCount each small step.

faq.a: Grade R to Grade 3 in South African schools. Learners are about 7 to 8 years old in Grade 2.
Informal units, metres and centimetres, kilograms and litres.

faq.q: How many cm in a metre?

items.q: How long is the pencil?
items.e: The pencil starts at 0 and ends at 6. So it is 6 cm long. Count the spaces, not the numbers.

items.e: The rubber starts at 0 and ends at 4. So it is 4 cm long. Count the spaces, not the numbers.

items.q: How long is the pencil?
items.e: The pencil starts at 2, not at 0. Count the spaces from 2 to 8: there are 6. Or work it out: 8 − 2 = 6. So it is 6 cm long.

items.q: How long is the rubber?
items.e: The rubber starts at 1, not at 0. Count the spaces from 1 to 5: there are 4. Or work it out: 5 − 1 = 4. So it is 4 cm long.

items.q: What is about 1 m long?
items.e: One big step is about 1 m. A metre stick is 1 m long.

items.q: About how long is a paper clip?
items.e: A paper clip is about 3 fingertips long, so it is about 3 cm. 3 m is about 3 big steps.

items.q: About how long is a crayon?
items.e: A crayon fits in your hand. That is about 9 cm. 9 m is about as long as a classroom.

items.q: About how long is a new pencil?
items.e: A new pencil is a bit longer than your hand. That is about 18 cm. 18 m is longer than a school bus.

items.q: About how wide is a classroom door?
items.e: A door is about as wide as one big step. That is about 1 m.

items.q: Which tool is best to measure the classroom?
items.e: The classroom is long. A metre stick is 1 m long, so you need only a few. A short ruler, cubes or a paper clip would take a very long time.

items.q: About how tall is a door?
items.e: A door is taller than a grown-up. It is about 2 metre sticks tall: 2 m.

items.q: About how tall is a Grade 2 learner?
items.e: A Grade 2 learner is a bit taller than a metre stick. 1 m is 100 cm, so about 120 cm makes sense.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of an apple?
items.e: An apple is light. It is about 100 grams. 100 kg is heavier than a grown-up.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of a bag of sugar?
items.e: A bag of sugar is about 1 kilogram. 1 g is about as heavy as a paper clip.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of a Grade 2 child?
items.e: A Grade 2 child is about 20 kilograms. 20 g is lighter than a bar of chocolate.

items.q: The scale shows a bag of potatoes. What is the mass?
items.e: Every mark has a number. The needle is right on 3. So it is 3 kg.

items.q: The scale shows a bag of pasta. What is the mass?
items.e: Every mark has a number. The needle is right on 200. So it is 200 g.

items.q: The scale shows a pumpkin. What is the mass?
items.e: Every mark has a number. The needle is right on 4. So it is 4 kg.

items.q: The scale shows a box of eggs. What is the mass?
items.e: Every mark has a number. The needle is right on 400. So it is 400 g.

items.q: The scale shows a bag of dog food. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up in 2s. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. Count on from 4: 5. So it is 5 kg.

items.q: The scale shows a watermelon. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up in 2s. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. Count on from 6: 7. So it is 7 kg.

items.q: The scale shows a box of books. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up in 2s. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. Count on from 8: 9. So it is 9 kg.

items.q: The scale shows a bar of chocolate. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up in 20s. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 g. Count on from 40: 50. So it is 50 g.

items.q: The scale shows a bag of sweets. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up in 20s. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 g. Count on from 80: 90. So it is 90 g.

items.q: The scale shows a block of cheese. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up in 200s. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 g. Count on from 200: 300. So it is 300 g.

items.q: The scale shows a bag of rice. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up in 200s. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 g. Count on from 400: 500. So it is 500 g.

items.q: The scale shows a bunch of bananas. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up in 200s. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 g. Count on from 600: 700. So it is 700 g.
The numbers go up in 5s. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. Count on from 10: 11, 12. So it is 12 kg.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Look at the tens. 4 tens is less than 5 tens, so 45 cm < 54 cm.

items.q: Which holds the most?
items.e: 1 litre = 1 000 mℓ. That is more than 500 mℓ. Look at the units, not just the numbers.

items.q: Which list goes from the shortest to the longest?
items.e: 9 is the smallest number and 21 is the biggest. So the order is 9 cm, 12 cm, 21 cm.

items.q: Which list goes from the lightest to the heaviest?
items.e: 5 is the smallest number and 50 is the biggest. So the order is 5 kg, 15 kg, 50 kg.

items.q: Which unit would you use to measure medicine on a spoon?
items.e: A spoon holds only a little. We measure a little water in millilitres (mℓ).

items.q: What is the best estimate for how much a cup holds?
items.e: A cup holds about 200 millilitres. 200 litres would fill a bath.

items.q: What is the best estimate for how much a bucket holds?
items.e: A bucket holds about 10 litres. 10 mℓ is only two teaspoons.

items.q: What is the best estimate for how much a teaspoon holds?
items.e: A teaspoon holds only a little, about 5 millilitres.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Every mark has a number. The water is right on 300. So it is 300 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Every mark has a number. The water is right on 2. So it is 2 litres.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up in 2s. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1 litre. Count on from 2: 3. So it is 3 litres.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?

items.e: The numbers go up in 20s. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 mℓ. The water is right on 40. So it is 40 mℓ.

items.e: The numbers go up in 20s. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 mℓ. Count on from 60: 70. So it is 70 mℓ.

items.e: The numbers go up in 200s. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 mℓ. Count on from 200: 300. So it is 300 mℓ.

items.e: The numbers go up in 200s. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 mℓ. Count on from 400: 500. So it is 500 mℓ.

items.e: The numbers go up in 200s. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 mℓ. Count on from 800: 900. So it is 900 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up in 10s. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 5 mℓ. Count on from 20: 25. So it is 25 mℓ.

items.q: About how long is a pencil?
items.e: A pencil fits on a ruler, so it is about 15 cm. 15 m is longer than a classroom!

items.q: Ethan has 45 cm of ribbon. He cuts off 20 cm. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Cutting off means take away: 45 − 20 = 25 cm.

items.q: Sibusiso has two pieces of string. One is 23 cm long. The other is 34 cm long. How much string is there altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add: 23 + 34 = 57 cm.

items.q: A sunflower is 60 cm tall. It grows 25 cm more. How tall is it now?
items.e: It grows, so add: 60 + 25 = 85 cm.

items.q: You measure with a ruler. Where do you put one end of the object?
c: at the edge of the ruler
items.e: Put the end at 0. Some rulers have a little space before the 0, so do not use the edge. If you start at 1, the number at the end is 1 too big.

items.q: How long is the rubber?
items.e: The rubber starts at 0 and ends at 3. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 cm long. Do not count the marks: there are 4 marks, because the 0 mark is not a space.

items.q: Measure the paper clip. How long is it?
items.e: The paper clip starts at 0 and ends at 3. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 cm long. Do not count the marks: there are 4 marks, because the 0 mark is not a space.

items.q: How long is the crayon?
items.e: The crayon starts at 0 and ends at 5. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. It is 5 cm long. Do not count the marks: there are 6 marks, because the 0 mark is not a space.

items.q: Measure the caterpillar. How long is it?
items.e: The caterpillar starts at 0 and ends at 7. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. It is 7 cm long. Do not count the marks: there are 8 marks, because the 0 mark is not a space.

items.q: How long is the worm?
items.e: The worm starts at 0 and ends at 8. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. It is 8 cm long. Do not count the marks: there are 9 marks, because the 0 mark is not a space.

items.q: What do you count to find a length on a ruler?
c: the last number on the ruler
items.e: Each space from one mark to the next is 1 cm. Count the spaces, not the marks. A 3 cm rubber covers 3 spaces but touches 4 marks.

items.q: Measure the straw. How long is it?
items.e: The straw starts at 0 and ends at 10. It is 10 cm long. Do not count the marks: there are 11 marks, because the 0 mark is not a space.

items.q: How long is the marker?
items.e: The marker starts at 0 and ends at 11. It is 11 cm long. Do not count the marks: there are 12 marks, because the 0 mark is not a space.

items.q: Measure the pencil. How long is it?
items.e: The pencil starts at 0 and ends at 13. It is 13 cm long. Do not count the marks: there are 14 marks, because the 0 mark is not a space.

items.q: How long is the rubber?
items.e: The rubber starts at 1, not at 0. Count on from 1: 2, 3, 4. That is 3 spaces. Or subtract: 4 − 1 = 3. So it is 3 cm long. 4 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: How long is the key?
items.e: The key starts at 3, not at 0. Count on from 3: 4, 5, 6. That is 3 spaces. Or subtract: 6 − 3 = 3. So it is 3 cm long. 6 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: The end of Nomsa’s ruler broke off, so it starts at 4. She puts a paper clip at the 4. The paper clip ends at 7. How long is it?
items.e: Count from 4, not from 0: 5, 6, 7 is 3 spaces. 7 − 4 = 3, so the paper clip is 3 cm long.

items.q: How long is the caterpillar?
items.e: The caterpillar starts at 4, not at 0. Count on from 4: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. That is 5 spaces. Or subtract: 9 − 4 = 5. So it is 5 cm long. 9 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: How long is the marker?
items.e: The marker starts at 2, not at 0. Subtract: 10 − 2 = 8. So it is 8 cm long. 10 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: Kabelo’s ruler starts at 3 because the end is broken. A marker starts at 3 and ends at 11. How long is the marker?
items.e: Subtract the start from the end: 11 − 3 = 8. The marker is 8 cm long.

items.q: How long is the straw?
items.e: The straw starts at 3, not at 0. Subtract: 12 − 3 = 9. So it is 9 cm long. 12 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: Daniel puts the end of a crayon at 1, not at 0. The other end is at 9. He says the crayon is 9 cm. What did he do wrong?
items.e: The crayon starts at 1, so 9 is too big. Count from 1 to 9: 9 − 1 = 8. The crayon is 8 cm long.

items.q: A pencil starts at 3 and ends at 12 on a ruler. Busisiwe counts the marks from 3 to 12 and gets 10. How long is the pencil?
items.e: Count spaces, not marks. From 3 to 12 there are 10 marks but only 9 spaces. 12 − 3 = 9, so the pencil is 9 cm long.

items.q: How long is the craft stick?
items.e: The craft stick starts at 5, not at 0. Subtract: 14 − 5 = 9. So it is 9 cm long. 14 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: Johan has 45 cm of ribbon. He cuts off 20 cm. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Cutting off means take away: 45 − 20 = 25 cm.

items.q: Mpho has two pieces of string. One is 23 cm long. The other is 34 cm long. How much string is there altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add: 23 + 34 = 57 cm.

items.q: Liam builds a tower 48 cm tall. Mbali builds a tower 30 cm tall. How much taller is Liam’s tower?
items.e: How much taller means find the difference: 48 − 30 = 18 cm.

items.q: A cat weighs 4 kg. A dog weighs 12 kg. How much heavier is the dog?
items.e: Find the difference: 12 − 4 = 8 kg.

items.q: Sipho has a 500 mℓ bottle of water. He drinks 200 mℓ at lunchtime. How much water is left?
items.e: Drinks means take away: 500 − 200 = 300 mℓ.

items.q: A bucket holds 5 litres. How much water do 4 buckets hold?
items.e: 4 lots of 5 litres: 5, 10, 15, 20. So 4 × 5 = 20 litres.

items.q: Lethabo fills a 10 litre paddling pool with a 2 litre jug. How many jugs of water does he need?
items.e: How many 2s make 10? Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. That is 5 jugs. 10 ÷ 2 = 5.

items.q: In the morning it was 8 °C. At lunchtime it was 15 °C. How many degrees warmer was it at lunchtime?
items.e: Find the difference. Count on from 8 to 15: 8 to 10 is 2, 10 to 15 is 5. 2 + 5 = 7 °C.

items.q: In the afternoon it was 21 °C. In the evening it was 6 degrees colder. What was the temperature in the evening?
items.e: Colder means take away: 21 − 6 = 15 °C.

items.q: Karabo has 45 cm of ribbon. She cuts off 20 cm. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Cutting off means take away: 45 − 20 = 25 cm.

items.q: Lethabo has two pieces of string. One is 23 cm long. The other is 34 cm long. How much string is there altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add: 23 + 34 = 57 cm.

items.q: Mpho builds a tower 48 cm tall. Aisha builds a tower 30 cm tall. How much taller is Mpho’s tower?
items.e: How much taller means find the difference: 48 − 30 = 18 cm.

items.q: How much longer is the pencil than the crayon?
items.e: Both start at 0. The pencil ends at 12 and the crayon ends at 7. 12 − 7 = 5. The pencil is 5 cm longer.

items.q: How much longer is the straw than the rubber?
items.e: Both start at 0. The straw ends at 10 and the rubber ends at 3. 10 − 3 = 7. The straw is 7 cm longer.

items.q: How much longer is the ribbon than the key?
items.e: Both start at 0. The ribbon ends at 15 and the key ends at 6. 15 − 6 = 9. The ribbon is 9 cm longer.

items.q: How much longer is the marker than the caterpillar?
items.e: Both start at 0. The marker ends at 11 and the caterpillar ends at 5. 11 − 5 = 6. The marker is 6 cm longer.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: The straw goes from 0 to 7: 7 cm. The pencil goes from 5 to 11: 11 − 5 = 6 cm. The straw is longer, even though the pencil ends at a bigger number.

items.q: Which length is the longest?
items.e: 1 m is 100 cm. 100 cm is more than 90, 60 or 45 cm, so 1 m is the longest.

items.q: Tebogo found two worms. One is 12 cm long. The other is 7 cm long. How much longer is the long worm?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 12 − 7 = 5 cm. Or count on from 7 to 12: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. Do not add: 12 + 7 = 19 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: Chloe’s paper airplane flew 9 m. Lethabo’s flew 6 m. How much farther did Chloe’s airplane fly?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 9 − 6 = 3 m. Or count on from 6 to 9: 7, 8, 9. Do not add: 9 + 6 = 15 is the total, not the difference.
